item.title: CView: Crystal Structure Visualization & Analysis
item.description:
Why CView?

In computational materials science, visualizing large supercells or complex lattice structures often requires heavy GUI-based software that breaks the terminal-based workflow.

CView bridges this gap. It is built to be lightweight, fast, and integrable directly into your command-line environment, allowing you to inspect structures without leaving your terminal.

Key Capabilities

  • High-Fidelity Rendering: Optimized for clarity, even with dense atomic structures.
  • Workflow Integration: works alongside standard tools (like VASP, Quantum ESPRESSO) to visualize outputs instantly.
  • Lightweight Footprint: No heavy GUI overhead; designed for speed and efficiency on clusters and local machines.

Quick Start

Get up and running in seconds. Clone the repository and install dependencies:

git clone https://github.com/mavensgroup/cview.git
cd cview
# Install command (You mostly need rust and gtk4-devel)
cargo run --release

item.title: MkBib: Bibliography Manager
item.description:
Why mkbib?

Managing citations is often the bottleneck of academic writing. Inconsistent formatting, missing fields, and duplicate entries can clutter your .bib files and cause compilation errors.

mkbib solves this by automating the hygiene of your bibliography. It ensures your references are publication-ready so you can focus on the content, not the metadata.

Key Capabilities

  • Automated Cleaning: Standardizes entry formats and corrects common syntax errors automatically.
  • Duplicate Detection: Intelligently identifies and merges or flags duplicate citations.
  • Pipeline Ready: Designed to fit into Makefiles or CI/CD pipelines for automated LaTeX document generation.

Quick Start

Integrate mkbib into your writing workflow:

git clone https://github.com/mavens-group/mkbib.git
cd mkbib
# Install command (You mostly need rust and gtk4-devel)
cargo run --release

item.title: Ptbl: Periodic Table
item.description:
What it does

Ptbl is a periodic table for the Linux desktop, built with GTK 4 and libadwaita. It works offline.

  • Browse all 118 elements, coloured by category, with up to 40 properties per element on six tabs.
  • Search and filter: find an element by symbol or name as you type, or highlight one category, such as the transition metals.
  • Colour by property: turn the table into a heatmap of one of eight properties.
  • Trend charts: plot atomic, covalent or van der Waals radius, or electron affinity, against atomic number.
  • Vegard’s law calculator: estimate the lattice parameters, cell volume and density of an alloy from its composition, then open the structure in CView or export it as a CIF file.

Atomic and thermal properties come from a bundled snapshot of the PubChem periodic table. Some crystal, electrical, magnetic and nuclear values come from earlier versions of Ptbl and haven’t yet been checked against current sources, so verify them before relying on them. Vegard’s-law results are quick estimates, not a substitute for a calculation or a measurement.

Quick Start

Ptbl needs Linux, Python 3.10 or newer, and GTK 4.12, libadwaita 1.5 and PyGObject from your distribution’s packages (on Fedora: sudo dnf install gtk4 libadwaita python3-gobject).

python3 -m pip install --user git+https://github.com/mavens-group/Ptbl.git
ptbl

On Debian, Ubuntu and Arch Linux, add --break-system-packages. The README covers every distribution, virtual environments and troubleshooting.
